name: Rice (Paddy)
soilType: Deep clayey and alluvial soils with high water-retention capacity
sunlight: Full sunlight; minimum 6 hours daily direct solar radiation

stages.description: Mat nursery or wet nursery sprouting; 4-leaf stage ready for transplantation.
Primary and secondary tillers emerge; panicle initiation begins.
Exsertion of panicles and anthesis with high humidity requirement.
Milky endosperm hardens into firm golden paddy grains.

funFact: Thanjavur and the Cauvery Delta region form the ancient 'Rice Bowl of Tamil Nadu', cultivating famous heritage rice varieties like Seeraga Samba and Ponni!
basicPractices: Maintain 2–5 cm water ponding during vegetative tillering phase.
Apply balanced NPK with split nitrogen applications to prevent lodging.
Incorporate green manure (Daincha or Sunnhemp) 15 days before puddling.
Use certified TNAU seeds like CR 1009 Sub-1, CO 51, and ADT 45.
symptoms: Spindle-shaped elliptical lesions with gray-white centers and brownish margins on leaf blades
Neck rot at panicle base resulting in completely empty, chaffy white ears ('Neck Blast')
Rapid lesion coalescence under high humidity causing complete foliar scorching
cause: Airborne fungal pathogen Magnaporthe oryzae proliferating in night temperatures of 20-24°C with relative humidity >90% and excessive nitrogen fertilisation.
prevention: Seed treatment with Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 2.0 g/kg seed
Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 ml/L at tillering
Avoid excessive single-dose urea application; use leaf color chart (LCC)
Adopt resistant varieties like ADT 43, CO 51, and ASD 16

name: Maize
soilType: Deep, fertile, well-drained sandy loam rich in organic matter
sunlight: Intense sunlight; C4 photosynthetic plant with exceptional solar efficiency

stages.description: Rapid germination; distinct whorl leaves unfold from the central growing point.
Terminal male inflorescence (tassel) sheds pollen granules.
Silks emerge from ear shoots to intercept pollen grains for ovule fertilisation.
Kernels pack starch; black layer forms at base of mature grain.

funFact: Perambalur is celebrated as the 'Maize Capital of Tamil Nadu', producing prime grain for poultry feed and bio-starch processing!
basicPractices: Adopt ridge and furrow planting spaced 60 x 20 cm.
Install pheromone traps @ 12/ha to monitor Fall Armyworm moths.
Apply zinc sulphate @ 25 kg/ha basal to avoid white bud deficiency.
Provide critical irrigations at tasseling and silking stages.
symptoms: Golden-brown to cinnamon-brown powdery pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture epidermal tissue, shedding millions of urediniospores
Premature chlorosis and drying of foliage, reducing cob filling
cause: Airborne fungal spores of Puccinia sorghi carried by wind during cool, moist weather (16-25°C).
prevention: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L at the first sign of pustules
Ensure balanced NPK nutrition; avoid excess nitrogen and supply adequate potash
Grow tolerant hybrid varieties recommended by TNAU (CO 6, COH(M) 8)

name: Wheat
soilType: Well-drained rich clay loams and silt loams with neutral pH
sunlight: Bright sunshine with cool nights during vegetative and tillering phases

stages.description: Crown roots anchor the seedling; most critical irrigation stage.
Secondary tillers form and stem nodes elongate upward.
Spikes emerge; pollination occurs inside glumes.
Kernel moisture drops below 14%; spikes turn golden-straw.

funFact: Wheat in Tamil Nadu is traditionally grown in the temperate high-altitude regions of the Nilgiris and Palani hills, prized for artisanal flour milling!
basicPractices: Irrigate precisely at Crown Root Initiation (21 DAS) and flowering stages.
Treat seed with Carboxin 75% WP @ 2.0 g/kg seed to prevent smut.
Maintain soil organic carbon with compost additions before sowing.
symptoms: Reddish-brown to dark elongated pustules erupting through stem and leaf sheaths
Torn epidermal fringes surrounding necrotic rust pustules
Stems weaken, causing catastrophic lodging of ripe wheat ears
cause: Fungal pathogen Puccinia graminis thriving under warm days (20-30°C) with moist dew.
prevention: Foliar spray of Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1.0 ml/L at onset
Cultivate rust-resistant varieties verified by Wellington Regional Research Station (IARI)
Avoid late sowing to bypass peak rust sporulation periods

name: Pearl Millet (Kambu)
soilType: Light sandy loams, gravelly red soils, and marginal rainfed tracts
sunlight: High solar radiation; exceptional drought tolerance and heat endurance

stages.description: Rapid germination even in semi-arid soils; deep taproot anchors.
Multiple basal tillers produce thick solid canes.
Cylindrical compact floral heads emerge, showing protogynous stigmas.
Small grey-pearl grains harden inside bristles; ready for harvest.

funFact: 'Kambu Koozh' (fermented pearl millet porridge) is Tamil Nadu's traditional natural cooling summer drink, celebrated for its high iron and calcium content!
basicPractices: Sow in rows 45 x 15 cm with 5 kg seed/ha treated with bio-fertilizers.
Intercrop with cowpea or green gram in 4:1 ratio for risk diversification.
Apply Azospirillum and Phosphobacteria @ 2 kg/ha mixed with FYM.
symptoms: Chlorotic yellow-green striping along leaf blades from base to tip
Downy white fungal growth on lower leaf surfaces under morning humidity
Floral parts in the earhead transform into twisted leafy structures ('Green Ear')
cause: Soil-borne and seed-borne oomycete Sclerospora graminicola with persistent oospores.
prevention: Seed dressing with Metalaxyl 35% WS @ 6.0 g/kg seed
Foliar spray with Metalaxyl-Mancozeb @ 2.0 g/L at 20 DAS if symptoms appear
Rogue out and burn infected plants early to prevent soil oospore accumulation

name: Finger Millet (Ragi)
soilType: Red loamy, sandy, and laterite soils with good internal drainage
sunlight: Bright tropical sun; tolerates moderate shade and intermittent drought

stages.description: Transplanted 21-day seedlings establish fibrous root mat.
Produces 4 to 8 productive culms per hill.
Whirled digital fingers (4 to 7 spikes) spread like hand fingers.
Globular reddish-brown grains turn dark and dry out.

funFact: Finger millet contains ten times more calcium than rice or wheat, making 'Ragi Kali' and 'Ragi Dosa' staple superfoods across rural Tamil Nadu!
basicPractices: Transplant 3-week-old seedlings spaced 22.5 x 10 cm for maximum tillering.
Apply 10 tonnes FYM/ha alongside 60:30:30 kg NPK/ha.
Weed at 15 and 30 DAT to prevent canopy choking.
symptoms: Spindle-shaped lesions with ashy-grey centers and dark brown margins on leaves
Black ring necrosis on neck of the fingers ('Neck Blast'), preventing grain fill
Bending and snapping of earhead at finger junctions
cause: Airborne fungal pathogen Magnaporthe grisea favored by cool humid nights and cloudy days.
prevention: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/kg seed
Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L or Kitazin 48% EC @ 2.0 ml/L at heading
Cultivate resistant varieties like GPU 28, CO (Ra) 14, and Paiyur 2

name: Sorghum (Cholam)
soilType: Clayey black cotton soils (vertisols) and deep red loams
sunlight: High solar exposure; remarkable drought-dormancy mechanism

stages.description: Rapid deep taproot system penetrates up to 1.5 meters deep.
Thick juicy culm develops waxy cuticle on leaf sheaths.
Large branched terminal panicle emerges from the boot leaf.
Round grains ripen from milky white to pearly cream or red.

funFact: Sorghum stalks are so rich in natural sweet carbohydrates that Tamil Nadu livestock farmers value the green fodder as much as the harvested grain!
basicPractices: Sow in flat beds or ridges spaced 45 x 15 cm with 10 kg seed/ha.
Thin seedlings at 15 DAS leaving one vigorous seedling per hill.
Provide one life-saving irrigation at boot leaf stage during dry spells.
symptoms: Circular to elliptical red or purplish spots with central straw-colored necrosis
Black minute fruiting bodies (acervuli) visible in concentric rings inside spots
Internal stalk pith turns crimson red when stem rot occurs
cause: Fungal pathogen Colletotrichum sublineolum spreading via rain splash during warm humid spells.
prevention: Seed treatment with Thiram or Captan @ 3.0 g/kg seed
Spray Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L or Mancozeb @ 2.0 g/L at first appearance
Adopt balanced fertilisation avoiding excess nitrogen

name: Green Gram (Pachai Payaru)
soilType: Well-drained loams and red clay soils; intolerant of waterlogging
sunlight: Full sun; fixes atmospheric nitrogen through root nodule Rhizobium

stages.description: Epigeal emergence; active Rhizobia nodulate taproot.
Trifoliate leaves proliferate, forming a compact bushy canopy.
Bright yellow self-pollinating flowers open in terminal clusters.
Slender pods turn from green to black; ready for split harvests.

funFact: Green gram is the superstar 'Rice Fallow Pulse' of the Cauvery Delta, sown into standing paddy stubbles 5 days before harvest to utilize residual soil moisture!
basicPractices: Treat seeds with Rhizobium culture (CO 1) @ 600 g/ha to boost root nodules.
Broadcast in standing rice crop at 25 kg/ha seed rate.
Foliar spray 2% DAP at flower initiation and 15 days later to boost pod set.
symptoms: Vibrant bright yellow irregular patches alternating with green on leaflets
Complete chlorosis of leaves, turning leaves golden-yellow and brittle
Severe stunting with few, deformed pods containing shrivelled seeds
cause: Geminivirus transmitted by the whitefly vector (Bemisia tabaci).
prevention: Seed treatment with Imidacloprid 70% WS @ 5.0 ml/kg seed
Spray Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3 g/L or Dimethoate 30% EC @ 1.7 ml/L to control whiteflies
Install yellow sticky traps @ 12 traps/ha in the field
Cultivate MYMV-resistant varieties like VBN (Gg) 2 and VBN (Gg) 3

name: Black Gram (Ulundhu)
soilType: Loamy to heavy black cotton soils with good moisture retention
sunlight: Direct tropical solar irradiance; fixes 40 kg N/ha naturally

stages.description: Rapid germination; nitrogen-fixing bacterial colonies establish.
Densely pubescent stems and hairy trifoliate leaves develop.
Yellow blossoms set hairy cylindrical pods.
Pods turn charcoal black; seeds achieve characteristic high mucilage.

funFact: Black gram provides the essential gelatinous mucilage protein required to naturally ferment authentic Tamil Nadu Idli and Medu Vada batters!
basicPractices: Treat seed with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg + Rhizobium @ 25 g/kg.
Spray 2% DAP or TNAU Pulse Wonder @ 5 kg/ha at flowering to halt flower drop.
Dry pods thoroughly to 10% moisture before mechanical threshing.
symptoms: Sudden wilting and drooping of top leaves during dry, sunny spells
Black dry rot lesions encircling the collar and taproot region
Minute black sclerotia visible beneath shredded bark of dead taproots
cause: Soil-borne fungus Macrophomina phaseolina attacking moisture-stressed roots.
prevention: Soil application of Trichoderma viride @ 2.5 kg/ha mixed with 50 kg well-decomposed FYM
Seed treatment with Carbendazim @ 2.0 g/kg seed
Avoid prolonged soil moisture stress during pod development

name: Red Gram (Thuvaram Paruppu)
soilType: Deep, well-drained loams and red laterites with deep subsoil permeability
sunlight: Full direct sunlight; deep taproots mine water from 2 meters depth

stages.description: Slow initial top growth while deep taproot establishes.
Develops into a woody perennial-like shrub 1.5 to 2.5 meters tall.
Abundant yellow and orange-veined flowers attract pollinators.
Flattish hairy pods ripen; beans yield nutritious dhal.

funFact: Red gram dhal is the indispensable culinary heart of Tamil Nadu 'Sambar', providing essential protein to millions of households daily!
basicPractices: Nip apical terminal shoots at 45 DAS to induce profuse lateral branches.
Intercrop with groundnut or ragi in 1:6 ratio for higher economic returns.
Install pheromone traps for Helicoverpa pod borer monitoring.
symptoms: Mosaic mottling, vein clearing, and severe reduction in leaflet size
Bushy, stunted vegetative growth with excessive secondary branching
Complete absence of flowers or pods; plants remain entirely sterile
cause: Tenuivirus transmitted by the microscopic eriophyid mite (Aceria cajani).
prevention: Spray Fenazaquin 10% EC @ 1.5 ml/L or Wettable Sulphur @ 3.0 g/L to control mite vectors
Rogue out infected plants immediately upon first sighting in early stages
Cultivate SMD-resistant varieties like VBN (Rg) 3, CO 7, and BSR 1

name: Groundnut
soilType: Light, friable, loose sandy loam rich in calcium; compacted soils impede pegging
sunlight: Full direct sunlight; minimum 7 hours daily solar irradiance

stages.description: Quadrifoliate leaves emerge; lateral branches spread close to ground.
Bright golden-yellow self-pollinating flowers bloom at dawn.
Fertilised flower stems (pegs) bend downward and penetrate 3–5 cm into soil.
Peg tips swell horizontally into two-seeded fibrous pods underground.

funFact: Tiruvannamalai and Villupuram are Tamil Nadu's groundnut heartlands, operating thousands of traditional stone cold-presses (Mara Chekku) for pure unrefined oil!
basicPractices: Apply Gypsum @ 400 kg/ha at 40–45 DAS (flowering/pegging) to supply essential calcium for pod filling.
Avoid earthing up or disturbing soil after peg penetration has begun.
Treat seed with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg seed to prevent collar rot.
symptoms: Small, circular to irregular dark brown to black necrotic spots on leaves
Prominent bright yellow chlorotic halos encircling dark lesions
Premature defoliation leaving stems completely bare, impairing pod bulking
cause: Fungal pathogens thriving in warm temperatures (25-30°C) with high humidity and prolonged leaf wetness.
prevention: Spray Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Mancozeb @ 2.0 g/L at 40 and 55 DAS
Spray Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP @ 1.5 g/L if disease spreads rapidly
Adopt crop rotation with non-legumes like sorghum or maize

name: Cotton
soilType: Deep black cotton soils (vertisols) and fertile deep clay loams
sunlight: Long sunny warm days; sensitive to frost and waterlogging

stages.description: Forms monopodial (vegetative) and sympodial (fruiting) branches.
Pyramidal floral buds (squares) develop inside protective bracts.
Cream blossoms turn pink post-pollination; spherical green bolls form.
Mature bolls dehisce, revealing pure white cellulosic lint fiber.

funFact: Coimbatore is historically hailed as the 'Manchester of South India' due to hundreds of textile mills fueled by Tamil Nadu cotton farming!
basicPractices: Maintain plant geometry of 90 x 45 cm for hybrid varieties.
Spray 1% Magnesium Sulphate + 1% Urea at 60 and 90 DAS to prevent leaf reddening.
Install pheromone traps @ 12/ha to track Pink Bollworm infestations.
symptoms: Angular, water-soaked, vein-bounded brown lesions on the foliage
Black elongated lesions on stems and petioles causing stem snapping ('Black Arm')
Water-soaked circular dark lesions on green bolls causing premature drop
cause: Seed-borne and rain-splashed bacterium Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum.
prevention: Acid delinting of seeds with concentrated H2SO4 @ 100 ml/kg seed
Foliar spray of Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L + Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L
Maintain field sanitation and destroy post-harvest cotton stalks

name: Sugarcane
soilType: Deep, well-drained, rich alluvial loams and heavy clay loams
sunlight: High solar radiation; exceptional C4 photosynthetic efficiency

stages.description: Two-budded setts sprout underground; primary roots anchor.
Clump tillers multiply; earthing-up provides mechanical support.
Rapid internode elongation; culms accumulate sucrose juice.
Vegetative growth slows; sucrose content peaks across stalk nodes.

funFact: Sugarcane is the sacred centerpiece of the harvest festival 'Pongal' in Tamil Nadu, where whole stalks are tied around earthen cooking pots to welcome prosperity!
basicPractices: Plant two-budded setts treated with Carbendazim 0.1% in deep furrows.
Adopt wide-row planting (150 cm spacing) with subsurface drip fertigation.
Perform de-trashing of dry lower leaves at 5th and 7th months to improve aeration.
symptoms: Third or fourth leaf from the top turns yellow, droops, and withers along margins
Internal pith reveals deep blood-red discoloration with diagnostic white cross-bands
Split stalks emit a distinct sour alcoholic fermentation odor
cause: Sett-borne and water-borne fungus Colletotrichum falcatum entering through root primordia or borer holes.
prevention: Dip setts in Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L for 15 minutes before planting
Rogue out and incinerate infected clumps with root systems
Use certified disease-free tissue culture seed setts (CoC 24, Co 86032)

name: Sunflower
soilType: Deep, fertile, neutral black cotton soils and loamy soils
sunlight: High heliotropism; young floral buds track the sun from east to west daily

stages.description: Large cordate leaves arrange spirally on a thick bristly stalk.
Terminal inflorescence head appears surrounded by protective involucral bracts.
Golden ray florets encircle thousands of disk florets pollinated by bees.
Back of the capitulum turns lemon-yellow; seeds accumulate 40% premium oil.

funFact: Sunflowers exhibit natural heliotropism: young flower heads track the path of the sun from dawn to dusk to warm florets and attract pollinators!
basicPractices: Maintain honeybee hives @ 5 hives/ha to maximize cross-pollination and seed set.
Spray Borax @ 2.0 g/L at star bud stage to eliminate chaffy center seeds.
Space plants at 60 x 30 cm with one plant per hill.
symptoms: Dark brown circular to irregular spots with concentric rings on leaves
Lesions coalesce causing large necrotic patches and leaf drooping
Dark brown elongated lesions on stems and ray florets
cause: Seed-borne and airborne fungal pathogen Alternaria helianthi.
prevention: Seed treatment with Mancozeb @ 3.0 g/kg seed
Foliar spray with Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Propiconazole @ 1.0 ml/L at 45 DAS
Destroy infected crop residues after harvest

name: Sesame (Ellu)
soilType: Well-drained light sandy loams and red soils; extremely sensitive to standing water
sunlight: Abundant bright sunshine; drought-tolerant summer oilseed

stages.description: Minute seeds emerge; opposite leaves branch from square stems.
Bell-shaped white to pale pink flowers bloom in leaf axils.
Four-grooved erect capsules pack 60-80 oil-rich seeds each.
Lower leaves drop; capsules turn golden-yellow before bursting.

funFact: Sesame ('Nallennai' or good oil) is Tamil Nadu's traditional queen of cooking oils, and sesame sweets ('Ellu Urundai') are offered in ancient Tamil rituals!
basicPractices: Mix small seeds with fine sand (1:4 ratio) for uniform field broadcasting.
Thin seedlings strictly at 15 DAS maintaining 30 x 30 cm spacing.
Harvest promptly when lower capsules turn yellow to prevent seed shattering.
symptoms: Floral parts completely transform into green leafy structures (phyllody)
Severe shortening of internodes causing bushy 'witch's broom' top appearance
Capsules fail to form or produce sterile, hollow husks
cause: Phytoplasma organism transmitted by the leafhopper vector Orosius albicinctus.
prevention: Foliar spray with Dimethoate 30% EC @ 1.5 ml/L to control leafhopper vectors
Rogue out and destroy infected phyllody plants as soon as noticed
Grow tolerant varieties like TMV 3 and VRI 1

name: Coconut
soilType: Deep sandy loams, coastal alluvium, and red loams with high drainage
sunlight: Unobstructed tropical sunlight; thrives with warm coastal breeze and high humidity

stages.description: Fronds multiply; sturdy columnar trunk forms with robust root bole.
Spathe emerges in leaf axils containing thousands of male and female button flowers.
Fertilised buttons swell into green nuts filled with sweet electrolyte water.
Outer husk turns brown; endosperm solidifies into rich oily copra meat.

funFact: Pollachi in Coimbatore district is celebrated across India as the 'Coconut Capital', famous for tender coconuts, coir fiber industries, and lush coconut plantations!
basicPractices: Dig circular basin 1.8 m radius around palm base and apply 50 kg green manure annually.
Drip irrigate 80–100 litres of water per palm per day during dry summer months.
Apply 1.3 kg Urea, 2.0 kg Superphosphate, and 2.0 kg Muriate of Potash per adult palm annually.
symptoms: Withering and yellowing of outer lower fronds, which droop and hang down around the trunk
Reddish-brown viscous bleeding fluid oozing from cracks at the base of the stem up to 1.5 meters
Decay of basal bole tissues and emergence of bracket-like fungal conks
cause: Soil-borne bracket fungus Ganoderma lucidum attacking roots and vascular vessels.
prevention: Root feeding with Hexaconazole 5% SC @ 2.0 ml in 100 ml water thrice a year
Apply 5 kg neem cake + Trichoderma viride @ 50 g/palm/year around trunk basin
Isolate diseased palms by digging isolation trenches (1 m deep, 30 cm wide)

name: Tomato
soilType: Well-aerated sandy loam with pH 6.0 – 6.8
sunlight: Minimum 7 hours of direct unobstructed sunshine

stages.description: Cotyledons expand followed by true leaves; ready for transplanting.
Deep taproot system and lateral branches proliferate.
Self-pollinating yellow blossoms buzz-pollinated by bees or wind.
Lycopene synthesis turns berries from green to deep radiant crimson.

funFact: Dharmapuri and Krishnagiri are known as the tomato hubs of Tamil Nadu, harvesting thousands of tonnes daily for Chennai and Bangalore markets!
basicPractices: Stake indeterminate tomato vines with bamboo poles to avoid soil-borne spore contamination.
Mulch with silver-black polyethylene film to conserve moisture and suppress weeds.
Spray micro-nutrients (Boron and Calcium) at flowering to avoid blossom end rot.
symptoms: Concentric dark brown 'target board' rings with surrounding chlorotic yellow halos on older leaves
Lesions progressively spread upward through the canopy, causing premature leaf drop
Sunscald risk on developing fruits due to loss of protective foliar shade
cause: Airborne and splash-dispersed fungal pathogen Alternaria solani thriving in temperatures of 24-29°C with high humidity.
prevention: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Chlorothalonil @ 2.0 g/L at 10-day intervals
Use drip irrigation rather than overhead sprinklers to keep foliage dry
Remove and destroy lower infected leaves 15 cm above ground level

name: Potato
soilType: Loose, friable sandy loam rich in humus; stones impede tuber expansion
sunlight: Full daylight for foliage; tubers require darkness to avoid toxic solanine

stages.description: Seed eyes sprout underground utilizing stored tuber nutrients.
Leaves emerge, photosynthesizing nutrients for stolon formation.
Stolon tips swell into miniature immature tubers underground.
Tubers accumulate starch; skin hardens after top vine senescence.

funFact: Ooty (Nilgiris) has been the historic center for hill potato cultivation in Tamil Nadu since British introduction in the 1820s!
basicPractices: Perform earthing-up at 30 and 50 DAP to cover developing tubers from sunlight exposure.
Plant certified disease-free seed tubers with 2–3 sprouted eyes.
De-haulm (cut top vines) 10 days before harvesting to harden tuber skin.
symptoms: Distinctive concentric target-board dark brown necrotic spots on potato leaves
Chlorotic yellow halos surrounding expanding necrotic lesions
Severe blight causes dry, papery brown leaves that remain attached to stems
cause: Fungal pathogen Alternaria solani attacking maturing potato foliage under alternating dry and wet weather.
prevention: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1.0 ml/L at onset
Maintain balanced potash nutrition to boost epidermal thickness
Rotate hill fields with French beans or garlic

name: Brinjal (Kathirikai)
soilType: Deep, rich loams and clay loams with neutral pH (6.5 – 7.5)
sunlight: Warm, sunny days; highly sensitive to cold frost

stages.description: Sturdy 5-leaf transplants ready for field planting.
Forms a dense spreading bush 60 to 100 cm tall.
Star-shaped violet flowers with yellow cone anthers bloom.
Glossy purple or green fruits harvested every 3–4 days.

funFact: Vellore's 'Mullu Kathirikai' (spiny brinjal) holds a prestigious Geographical Indication (GI) tag, celebrated for its buttery melt-in-mouth texture!
basicPractices: Space plants at 60 x 60 cm for bushy native cultivars.
Install yellow sticky traps @ 15/ha to monitor leafhopper vectors.
Apply neem cake @ 250 kg/ha to deter root-knot nematodes.
symptoms: Drastic reduction in leaf size; leaves become minute, soft, glabrous, and pale green
Severe shortening of internodes causing dense bushy appearance ('Witches Broom')
Floral parts turn green (phyllody) and become completely sterile without fruit set
cause: Phytoplasma organism transmitted by the leafhopper vector Hishimonus phycitis.
prevention: Rogue out and destroy infected little-leaf plants as soon as observed
Spray Dimethoate 30% EC @ 1.5 ml/L or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3 g/L to control leafhoppers
Dip roots of seedlings in Tetracycline hydrochloride solution (500 ppm) before transplanting

name: Chilli (Milagai)
soilType: Well-drained sandy loam and fertile black cotton soils
sunlight: Warm, sunny, dry climate during fruit ripening to develop high capsaicin

stages.description: Nursery grown seedlings transplanted into ridges.
Dichotomous branching with dark green glossy leaves.
Small white star flowers develop at node forks.
Slender pods turn from dark emerald green to fiery red.

funFact: Ramanathapuram's 'Mundu Chilli' (round cherry chilli) has a prestigious GI tag, treasured across Chettinad cuisine for its fiery pungency and rich red color!
basicPractices: Spray Azadirachtin 1% @ 2.0 ml/L to deter thrips that transmit leaf curl virus.
Avoid excessive irrigation during flowering to prevent blossom drop.
Dry harvested red chillies on clean tarpaulins under direct sun.
symptoms: Circular to oblong sunken necrotic spots on ripe red chillies with black concentric rings
Tip of young branches withers and dries downward ('Die-Back')
Fruits shrivel, bleach straw-white, and shed prematurely before harvest
cause: Seed-borne and airborne fungus Colletotrichum capsici spreading under humid, cloudy weather.
prevention: Seed treatment with Thiram or Captan @ 3.0 g/kg seed
Spray Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1.0 ml/L or Difenoconazole @ 0.5 ml/L during fruit set
Collect and destroy shrivelled infected chillies from the field

name: Onion (Vengayam)
soilType: Friable, fertile sandy loam and red loam with high organic matter and pH 6.0 – 7.0
sunlight: Clear sunny weather; photoperiod triggers bulb expansion

stages.description: Small onion sets (shallots) sprout hollow tubular green leaves.
Foliage multiplies, synthesizing sugars for bulb storage.
Leaf sheaths swell at soil line into distinct pungent clusters.
Tops naturally bend and collapse ('neck fall'); skin turns ruby pink.

funFact: Perambalur and Dindigul cultivate over 70% of South India's famous 'Chinna Vengayam' (small shallots), the essential soul of Tamil Nadu cooking!
basicPractices: Plant medium-sized healthy mother shallot bulbs spaced 15 x 10 cm.
Withhold irrigation 10 days before harvest to enhance storage shelf-life.
Cure harvested bulbs in shade for 7–10 days before market transport.
symptoms: Small, sunken, whitish lesions on tubular leaves turning purple to dark brown with yellow halo
Lesions girdle the leaf, causing the entire hollow blade to collapse and snap
Bulbs rot in storage if infection spreads down the neck
cause: Airborne fungus Alternaria porri proliferating under warm humid weather (25°C) with persistent dews.
prevention: Foliar spray with Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Tebuconazole @ 1.0 ml/L with sticker
Spray sticker (Triton / Sandovit @ 0.5 ml/L) to make spray adhere to waxy cylindrical onion leaves
Ensure field drainage to eliminate standing moisture

name: Ladies Finger (Vendakkai)
soilType: Rich, loose sandy loam and clay loam with good drainage
sunlight: Full hot sunshine; highly tolerant of tropical temperatures

stages.description: Hard-coated seeds germinate rapidly; broad lobed cotyledons open.
Sturdy hairy central stem produces palmate lobed leaves.
Large cream-yellow flowers with purple centers open at sunrise.
Tender mucilaginous pentagonal pods harvested every 2 days.

funFact: Ladies Finger is beloved for its natural soluble mucilage fiber, traditionally cooked into tangy Tamil Nadu 'Vendakkai Puli Kuzhambu'!
basicPractices: Soak seeds in water for 12 hours before sowing to soften seed coats.
Install yellow sticky traps @ 15/ha to manage whitefly vectors.
Harvest tender pods every alternate day before fibers harden.
symptoms: Veins of leaves turn bright golden-yellow while interveinal areas remain green
Complete network of yellow veins expands, turning entire leaf yellow and brittle
Fruits become dwarfed, yellowish-white, hard, and unmarketable
cause: Begomovirus transmitted persistently by the whitefly vector (Bemisia tabaci).
prevention: Grow resistant hybrid varieties like Arka Anamika, Parbhani Kranti, and CO 3
Spray Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3 g/L or Acetamiprid @ 0.2 g/L to suppress whiteflies
Rogue out early infected plants to halt field spread

name: Drumstick (Murungai)
soilType: Well-drained sandy loam, red soil, and alluvial soil; sensitive to waterlogging
sunlight: Full scorching sunlight; exceptionally drought-hardy miracle tree

stages.description: Rapid growth; develops soft woody stem and tripinnate compound leaves.
Terminal shoots pinched at 1 meter height to induce bushy lateral branching.
Clusters of sweet-scented white flowers bloom profusely.
Long pendulous green pods swell, packing protein and antioxidant seeds.

funFact: The Oddanchatram and Karur (Aravakurichi) belt of Tamil Nadu is India's leading exporter of drumsticks, prized worldwide for the famous 'PKM-1' and 'PKM-2' varieties!
basicPractices: Pinch terminal shoots at 75–90 cm height to encourage 8–10 lateral fruiting branches.
Spray neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) to repel the drumstick pod fly.
Apply 15 kg well-rotted FYM and 100 g urea per tree twice a year.
symptoms: Brown sunken spots on tender green drumstick pods that rapidly enlarge
Pods split open, gum oozes out, and pods rot from tip upward
Drying and withering of delicate white flower panicles
cause: Fungal pathogen Colletotrichum dematium spreading during damp monsoon conditions.
prevention: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Mancozeb @ 2.0 g/L at flowering
Prune overcrowded and dead branches after harvest to permit full sunlight penetration
Collect and destroy fallen rotten drumsticks from the orchard floor

name: Bitter Gourd (Pavakkai)
soilType: Deep sandy loam rich in organic manure with excellent drainage
sunlight: Warm, sunny weather; vines climb on pandal or bamboo trellises

stages.description: Tendrils coil around support wires, pulling five-lobed leaves upward.
Vigorous vine network carpets overhead wire trellis.
Distinct unisexual yellow flowers bloom with miniature spiny ovary on females.
Deep green ridged, warty fruits harvested every 3 days.

funFact: Bitter Gourd contains polypeptide-p and charantin, natural bioactive compounds widely researched for supporting healthy blood sugar levels in diabetes!
basicPractices: Erect overhead wire pandal (2 m height) for clean, straight, blemish-free gourds.
Install cue-lure traps @ 10/ha to trap melon fruit flies.
Drip irrigate at root zone to prevent foliar humidity and downy mildew.
symptoms: Angular yellow chlorotic lesions bounded strictly by leaf veins on upper leaf surface
Purplish-grey downy fungal felt on the corresponding lower leaf surface in morning dew
Leaves turn brown, curl upward, scorch, and drop prematurely
cause: Airborne oomycete Pseudoperonospora cubensis thriving under cool humid mornings (18-22°C).
prevention: Spray Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Metalaxyl-Mancozeb @ 2.0 g/L
Maintain trellis ventilation by pruning lower unproductive foliage
Avoid late evening overhead watering

name: Bottle Gourd (Suraikkai)
soilType: Rich loamy soils with high organic matter and good moisture retention
sunlight: Full sunshine; night-blooming white flowers pollinated by nocturnal moths

stages.description: Large pubescent cordate leaves climb vigorously.
Delicate white flowers open at dusk with sweet fragrance.
Smooth pale green gourds grow rapidly to 30–60 cm length.
Tender fruits harvested for cooking; mature ones dry into hard wooden vessels.

funFact: In ancient Tamil culture, hollow dried bottle gourd shells were cured to create musical instruments like the Tanpura and rustic water canteens!
basicPractices: Sow 3–4 seeds per pit in pits filled with 10 kg FYM + 100 g neem cake.
Train vines on pandal system to prevent ground rot and insect attacks.
Harvest when fruits are tender with soft skin that punctures easily with a fingernail.
symptoms: Circular, water-soaked, yellowish spots on leaves expanding into large brown lesions
Circular sunken water-soaked pits on the fruit surface that ooze pinkish spore masses
Shot-hole appearance on leaves as necrotic centers fall out
cause: Fungal pathogen Colletotrichum lagenarium spreading via rain splash during warm humid periods.
prevention: Foliar spray with Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L or Mancozeb @ 2.0 g/L at 14-day intervals
Treat seeds with Carbendazim @ 2.0 g/kg seed before sowing
Avoid mechanical bruising of fruits during harvest

name: Ridge Gourd (Peerkangai)
soilType: Fertile, loose, well-aerated sandy loam rich in organic compost
sunlight: Warm, sunny tropical days; climbs easily on trellises and fences

stages.description: Angular stems with strong tendrils climb trellises rapidly.
Yellow afternoon-blooming flowers attract honeybees.
Club-shaped green fruits develop 10 prominent longitudinal sharp ridges.
Tender fibrous gourds harvested; mature ones produce natural luffa bath sponges!

funFact: When fully mature and dried, the interior fibrous vascular skeleton of ridge gourd becomes the world-famous natural 'Luffa' exfoliating bath sponge!
basicPractices: Train vines on vertical string trellises or overhead pandal.
Apply micronutrient spray of Borax @ 1.0 g/L at flowering to prevent fruit curvature.
Harvest tender green fruits before interior vascular fibers harden.
symptoms: White talcum-powder like circular spots on both surfaces of leaves and stems
Powdery coating expands across entire leaf blade, impeding photosynthesis
Infected leaves turn brown, shrivel, curl downward, and drop prematurely
cause: Airborne fungus Erysiphe cichoracearum thriving in dry climates with high ambient humidity.
prevention: Spray Wettable Sulphur 80% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Dinocap @ 1.0 ml/L at initial symptom onset
Spray bio-fungicide Ampelomyces quisqualis @ 5.0 g/L
Maintain trellis spacing to permit direct sunlight penetration through canopy

name: Pumpkin (Poosanikai)
soilType: Deep sandy loam and fertile clay loam rich in organic matter
sunlight: Full direct sunshine; sprawling ground vine with massive leaves

stages.description: Extensive ground runners spread 5–10 meters with huge cordate leaves.
Large golden-yellow edible flowers bloom at dawn, pollinated by bumblebees.
Hefty ribbed fruits swell; flesh accumulates beta-carotene.
Rind hardens into thick orange-tan shell; stores for 6 months.

funFact: Pumpkin can store safely for over six months without refrigeration due to its thick waxy rind, serving as Tamil Nadu's traditional famine-reserve vegetable!
basicPractices: Dig pits 60 x 60 x 60 cm filled with 20 kg FYM and 100 g urea.
Mulch ground around vines with dry straw to prevent fruit rot in rainy weather.
Hand pollinate female flowers in early morning if bee activity is low.
symptoms: Severe yellow-green mottled mosaic patterns and blister-like leaf puckering
Distortion of leaf margins, filiform 'shoestring' leaves, and stunted vine growth
Fruits develop warty green bumps, mottled coloration, and bitter taste
cause: Potyvirus transmitted by aphid species (Aphis gossypii and Myzus persicae).
prevention: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5 ml/L or Dimethoate @ 1.5 ml/L to manage aphid vectors
Rogue out and destroy infected vines to halt spreading
Grow border barrier crops of maize or sorghum around the pumpkin field

name: Cucumber (Vellarikkai)
soilType: Loose, friable sandy loam with abundant compost and pH 6.0 – 7.0
sunlight: Warm, sunny tropical weather; 96% water content vegetable

stages.description: Rapid germination; two broad cotyledons emerge followed by true leaves.
Prostrate or climbing vines develop spiraling tendrils.
Bright yellow male flowers bloom first, followed by female flowers with miniature ovary.
Crisp cylindrical green fruits picked every morning.

funFact: Cucumbers are composed of 96% pure water and electrolytes, traditionally sliced and sprinkled with salt and chilli powder by Tamil Nadu street vendors as natural cooling snacks!
basicPractices: Maintain consistent soil moisture; water stress makes cucumbers develop bitter cucurbitacin.
Install pheromone cue-lure traps @ 10/ha to prevent fruit fly maggots.
Harvest fruits when crisp and bright green before seeds harden and yellow.
symptoms: Bright angular yellow chlorotic patches strictly bounded by veins on upper leaf surface
Purplish-brown velvety fungal down on lower surface under morning dew
Leaves curl, crisp like scorched paper, and drop, exposing fruits to sunburn
cause: Airborne oomycete pathogen thriving during warm days (24°C) with cool humid nights.
prevention: Foliar spray with Metalaxyl + Mancozeb @ 2.0 g/L or Fosetyl-Al @ 2.0 g/L
Avoid late evening irrigation; water at soil base via drip lines
Maintain trellis air circulation by thinning overcrowded lateral vines

name: Tapioca (Maravalli)
soilType: Deep, well-drained red sandy loam and alluvial soils with loose subsoil
sunlight: Full intense sunlight; remarkably drought-hardy root crop

stages.description: Stem cuttings (setts) sprout buds and adventitious root system.
Palmate leaves create dense canopy capturing solar energy.
Fibrous storage roots swell into thick cylindrical starchy tubers.
Lower leaves senesce; tubers reach maximum starch content.

funFact: Salem in Tamil Nadu is universally acclaimed as the 'Sago City of India', processing millions of tons of tapioca starch into sago (javvarisi) and industrial starch products!
basicPractices: Plant 15 cm long stem setts vertically or slightly slanting on ridges.
Use certified mosaic-free stem cuttings from verified healthy mother plants.
Apply potash @ 150 kg/ha in split doses to accelerate tuber starch accumulation.
symptoms: Severe yellow-green mosaic mottling on palmate leaf lobes with distorted crinkled margins
Leaf lobes become stunted, twisted, and asymmetrical, resembling deformed claws
Drastic reduction in plant vigor, tuber count, and starch content
cause: Geminivirus transmitted persistently by the whitefly vector (Bemisia tabaci) and through infected stem cuttings.
prevention: Select stem setts exclusively from CMD-free certified mother blocks
Spray Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3 g/L or Dimethoate @ 1.5 ml/L to control whiteflies
Rogue out and destroy infected sprouts within the first 60 days
Cultivate CMD-resistant varieties released by TNAU and CTCRI (YTP 1, Co 4)

name: Sweet Potato
soilType: Loose, friable sandy loam and light red soils; heavy clays induce misshapen tubers
sunlight: Bright, direct tropical sunshine; sprawling ground vine

stages.description: Terminal vine cuttings (20-25 cm) root vigorously at nodes.
Lush creeping heart-shaped foliage carpets ground, suppressing weeds.
Adventitious storage roots swell underground with beta-carotene.
Leaves yellow slightly; tubers lifted with hand forks without skin cuts.

funFact: Sweet potato tubers are packed with natural vitamin A (beta-carotene), traditionally boiled and seasoned with coconut and jaggery during Tamil winter festivals!
basicPractices: Plant terminal vine cuttings on ridges spaced 60 x 20 cm.
Earth-up at 30 and 50 DAP to cover developing tubers from sweet potato weevils.
Rotate fields with paddy or pulses to interrupt pest life cycles.
symptoms: Faint purple rings and chlorotic feather-like striping along principal leaf veins
General stunting and chlorotic yellowing of the trailing vine canopy
Cracked, grooved, or corky internal flesh inside storage roots
cause: Potyvirus transmitted non-persistently by aphid vectors (Aphis gossypii).
prevention: Use certified virus-tested tissue-culture vine cuttings
Spray systemic insecticide (Imidacloprid @ 0.5 ml/L) to suppress aphid populations
Dip vine cuttings in Carbendazim 0.1% before planting

name: Cluster Beans (Kothavarangai)
soilType: Well-drained sandy loam and alluvial soils with pH 7.0 – 8.5
sunlight: High solar exposure; exceptionally drought-hardy and heat-tolerant legume

stages.description: Rapid germination; deep taproot establishes nitrogen-fixing nodules.
Forms a stiff erect bushy plant 60–100 cm tall with trifoliate leaves.
Dense clusters of pink to bluish flowers bloom in leaf axils.
Flattish, fleshy green pods harvested in abundant clusters every 3 days.

funFact: Cluster bean seeds are the global source of natural 'Guar Gum', used worldwide as an emulsifier in ice creams, food sauces, and eco-friendly textiles!
basicPractices: Sow in rows spaced 45 x 15 cm with 10 kg seed/ha.
Treat seed with Rhizobium culture to enhance root nodulation.
Harvest tender, crisp pods before the seeds enlarge and fibers develop.
symptoms: Small water-soaked translucent circular spots on leaves that turn dark brown
Lesions expand along leaf margins causing V-shaped chlorotic blighting
Black streaks on stems causing stem splitting and defoliation
cause: Seed-borne bacterium Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. cyamopsidis spreading via rain splash during warm humid periods.
prevention: Hot water seed treatment at 56°C for 10 minutes before sowing
Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L + Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L at first symptom
Destroy infected crop residues after final harvest

name: Mango Tree (Maamaram)
soilType: Deep, fertile, well-drained alluvial and red sandy loam with deep water table
sunlight: Full hot tropical sunshine; rainless dry weather required during flowering

stages.description: Epicotyl or approach grafts form sturdy branching canopy.
Huge pyramidal inflorescences produce thousands of pinkish flowers.
Natural drop of unfertilised fruitlets; marble-sized mangoes set.
Shoulders round out; aroma develops; varieties turn golden yellow.

funFact: Krishnagiri and Dharmapuri are heralded as Tamil Nadu's 'Mango Capital', cultivating legendary varieties like Alphonso, Banganapalli, Salem Gundu, and Malgova!
basicPractices: Prune cross-branches and dead wood after harvest to permit sunlight into the center.
Spray Mancozeb @ 2 g/L or Azoxystrobin @ 1 ml/L before flowering panicles open.
Wrap developing fruits in newspaper bags to protect against fruit flies.
symptoms: Small dark brown circular necrotic spots on leaves that coalesce into irregular patches
Blackening and drop of entire blossom panicles ('Blossom Blight')
Tear-stain black streaks on ripening mango fruits that rot in storage
cause: Fungal pathogen Colletotrichum gloeosporioides favored by intermittent rains during flowering and fruit set.
prevention: Foliar spray with Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5 g/L or Carbendazim @ 1.0 g/L at panicle emergence
Hot water dip treatment of harvested mangoes at 52°C for 5 minutes before packing
Prune diseased twigs and spray Bordeaux mixture (1%) post-harvest

name: Banana Plant (Vaazhai)
soilType: Deep, rich, well-drained loams and alluvial soils with high organic matter and pH 6.5 – 7.5
sunlight: Bright, warm tropical sunshine; sheltered from cyclonic high winds

stages.description: Sword suckers or tissue culture plantlets sprout spiraling leaves.
Concentric leaf sheaths form a sturdy false trunk 2–4 meters tall.
Large purple floral bud (heart) emerges with spiraling female flower hands.
Hands of bananas swell; angles round out; ready for harvest.

funFact: Trichy is home to India's National Research Centre for Banana (NRCB), producing legendary Tamil Nadu cultivars like Grand Naine, Nendran, Poovan, Rasthali, and Red Banana!
basicPractices: Plant sword suckers treated with Carbendazim 0.1% or certified tissue-culture plantlets.
De-sucker regularly, allowing only one follower ratoon sucker per plant.
Provide propping support with bamboo poles as heavy bunches develop.
symptoms: Narrow, yellowish-green streaks parallel to leaf veins that expand into brown elliptical spots
Centers of lesions become sunken, dry, and ashy grey with dark brown borders
Extensive leaf blighting leaves the plant without enough green foliage to mature bunches
cause: Airborne ascospores of Mycosphaerella musicola proliferating under warm humid weather with rain showers.
prevention: Foliar spray with Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1.0 ml/L or Chlorothalonil @ 2.0 g/L with mineral oil (1%)
Cut and burn severely blighted lower leaves ('De-trashing')
Maintain wide spacing and proper trench drainage to lower canopy humidity

name: Lemon Tree (Elumichai)
soilType: Deep, fertile, well-drained sandy loam with pH 6.5 – 7.5; intolerant of hard pans
sunlight: Full bright sunshine; dry climate during ripening enhances citric acid

stages.description: Thorny branches develop with dark green ovate leaves and winged petioles.
Fragrant white blossoms with purple-tinted petals bloom in flushes.
Spherical green fruits expand, packing tart, vitamin C-rich juice.
Skin turns radiant yellow; essential citrus oil glands aromatic.

funFact: Puliangudi in Tenkasi district is acclaimed as the 'Lemon City of Tamil Nadu', harvesting thousands of tonnes of juicy lemons sent across India daily!
basicPractices: Prune water suckers and dead thorny twigs annually after harvest.
Apply micronutrients (Zinc, Iron, Manganese) foliar spray twice a year.
Paint tree trunk bases with Bordeaux paste to prevent fungal gummosis.
symptoms: Raised, blister-like corky necrotic brown eruptions on leaves, twigs, and fruits
Prominent oily water-soaked yellow halos surrounding corky lesions on leaves
Premature leaf drop and unmarketable blemished scabby fruit skin
cause: Bacterium Xanthomonas citri entering through stomata or leaf-miner insect wound punctures.
prevention: Spray Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L + Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5 g/L at 15-day intervals during new flush
Control leaf miners using Azadirachtin (Neem oil 1%) or Spinosad @ 0.4 ml/L
Prune and burn canker-infected twigs before the monsoon flush

name: Guava Tree (Koyya)
soilType: Versatile; tolerates shallow soils, red soils, and mild alkaline soils with pH 6.0 – 8.0
sunlight: Full direct sun; highly resilient to tropical heatwaves

stages.description: Smooth copper-colored peeling bark and opposite oblong leaves.
White flowers with hundreds of prominent tufted stamens bloom.
Globose to piriform fruits swell, packing vitamin C and fiber.
Skin turns from dark green to pale yellowish-green with sweet aroma.

funFact: Ayakudi near Palani is celebrated across Tamil Nadu as the 'Guava Capital', renowned for sweet, crisp, high-vitamin C cultivars like Lucknow-49 and Red Guava!
basicPractices: Perform light bending and pruning of branches to stimulate new flowering flushes.
Adopt Lucknow 49 (Sardar Guava) or Arka Kiran for high commercial yields.
Install methyl eugenol pheromone traps @ 10/ha to trap male fruit flies.
symptoms: Yellowing and browning of leaves on one branch, followed by rapid whole-tree wilting
Leaves turn dull, curl upward, and dry out while remaining attached to dead branches
Vascular discoloration: dark brown streaks visible inside split xylem wood
cause: Soil-borne fungal pathogen Fusarium oxysporum attacking roots through nematode wounds in alkaline soils.
prevention: Drench root zone with Carbendazim 0.2% or Copper Oxychloride 0.3% around affected basin
Incorporate neem cake @ 5 kg/tree + Trichoderma viride @ 50 g/tree into soil annually
Maintain soil drainage and avoid excessive soil compaction

name: Papaya
soilType: Deep, well-drained sandy loam rich in organic matter; extremely vulnerable to waterlogging
sunlight: Direct hot tropical sunshine; zero tolerance for stagnant surface water

stages.description: Grows into a single unbranched hollow fleshy stem with large palmate leaves.
Dioecious or gynodioecious flowers emerge in leaf axils.
Large oblong fruits cluster tightly along the upper trunk.
Skin turns golden-yellow; rich orange flesh accumulates papain and lycopene.

funFact: Coimbatore's TNAU pioneered the world-renowned 'CO 2' and 'CO 7' red-fleshed papayas, cultivated extensively for papain enzyme extraction used in pharmaceuticals!
basicPractices: Plant on high raised beds with trench drains to prevent deadly collar rot.
Spray micronutrient mixture containing Boron and Zinc to avoid fruit lumpy bumps.
Rogue out male plants in dioecious varieties maintaining 1 male for 10 females.
symptoms: Severe yellow-green mosaic mottling and leaf blister puckering on young crown leaves
Prominent dark green water-soaked oily streaks on petioles and upper trunk
Diagnostic concentric circular green ring spots on developing fruit skin
cause: Potyvirus transmitted non-persistently by aphid vectors (Aphis gossypii and Myzus persicae).
prevention: Plant border barrier rows of 3 lines of maize or sorghum 1 month before papaya planting
Spray Dimethoate @ 1.5 ml/L or Imidacloprid @ 0.5 ml/L to suppress aphids
Adopt TNAU-recommended cross-protection or tolerant varieties (Red Lady 786, CO 8)

name: Custard Apple (Seethapazham)
soilType: Extremely hardy; thrives in rocky, gravelly, marginal red soils and dry hill slopes
sunlight: Full blazing sun; naturally repellent to stray cattle and goats

stages.description: Semi-deciduous small tree with aromatic lanceolate leaves.
Fleshy three-petaled greenish flowers open with sweet fragrance.
Pellicle segments swell into a tuberculate aggregate fruit.
Grooves between segments turn creamy-white; fruit emits heavenly aroma.

funFact: Custard Apple leaves contain natural annonaceous acetogenins that are toxic to insects and cattle, making it virtually immune to stray animal grazing!
basicPractices: Space trees at 5 x 5 m on wasteland and rocky hill borders.
Spray Neem oil 2% to control white mealybugs that cluster between fruit segments.
Harvest fruits when the skin between the tuberculate segments turns creamy white.
symptoms: Dark brown to black sunken spots on leaves, flowers, and developing fruits
Fruits shrivel, mummify, turn jet-black, and remain hanging on the tree
Twig die-back and premature leaf shedding during rainy monsoon months
cause: Fungal pathogen Colletotrichum gloeosporioides spreading through rain splash under humid conditions.
prevention: Foliar spray with Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Carbendazim @ 1.0 g/L
Remove and destroy mummified dried black fruits from trees during annual pruning
Maintain open canopy architecture to permit morning breeze drying

name: Jackfruit Tree (Palaa)
soilType: Deep, fertile, well-drained alluvial and red laterite soils with deep subsoil
sunlight: Full direct tropical sunshine; high humidity accelerates fruit filling

stages.description: Grows into a massive evergreen tree with thick dark green leathery leaves.
Male and female flower spikes emerge directly from the main trunk and mature branches.
Giant aggregate fruits covered with conical spines swell up to 30 kg!
Spines flatten; fruit yields to pressure and emits intoxicating honey aroma.

funFact: Panruti in Cuddalore district is world-renowned as the 'Jackfruit Capital of Tamil Nadu', cultivating giant honey-sweet 'Thenkai Palaa' celebrated across ancient Sangam literature ('Mukkani')!
basicPractices: Plant grafts spaced 10 x 10 m in deep fertile pits.
Bag young fruits in woven nylon mesh or craft paper to prevent fruit flies and rot.
Apply 50 kg organic compost and 2 kg wood ash per tree before monsoon rains.
symptoms: Water-soaked soft brownish spots on young male flower spikes and tender fruitlets
Dense whisker-like black fungal mycelium and pinhead sporangia envelop the fruitlet
Tender fruits turn into mushy, rotting black pulp and drop off the trunk
cause: Wound-invading fungus Rhizopus stolonifer proliferating during warm rainy periods with high relative humidity (>85%).
prevention: Foliar spray with Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Mancozeb @ 2.0 g/L at early flowering
Remove and incinerate rotting male spikes and fallen fruitlets promptly
Thin overcrowded fruit clusters along the trunk to improve aeration

name: Sapota (Chikoo)
soilType: Deep sandy loam, alluvium, and red laterites; highly tolerant of coastal salt spray
sunlight: Warm, sunny, humid coastal and tropical climate

stages.description: Dense pyramidal evergreen canopy with glossy spirally arranged leaves.
Small bell-like white flowers bloom continuously in leaf axils.
Round or oval fruits develop sandy brown scurf skin packed with sweet latex.
Brown scurf rubs off revealing green skin underneath; pulp turns sweet malty brown.

funFact: Dindigul and Virudhunagar are Tamil Nadu's sapota hubs, cultivating the famous 'Cricket Ball' and 'PKM 1' varieties prized for their malty brown honey sweetness!
basicPractices: Cultivate high-yielding TNAU varieties like PKM 1, PKM 2, and Cricket Ball.
Scrape fruit skin lightly during harvest: if green underneath, the fruit is mature for harvest.
Spray Mancozeb @ 2 g/L to prevent fungal foliar leaf spots.
symptoms: Small circular to irregular dark purplish-brown spots on older leaves
Centers of older lesions turn whitish-grey with distinct dark margins
Severe spotting causes premature yellowing and dropping of functional leaves
cause: Fungal pathogen Phaeophleospora indica spreading during warm, rainy monsoon periods.
prevention: Foliar spray with Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Carbendazim @ 1.0 g/L
Prune congested internal branches to allow sunlight penetration
Collect and burn fallen spotted leaves

name: Pomegranate
soilType: Deep, well-drained loams and alluvial soils; tolerant of marginal and mild alkaline soils
sunlight: Hot, dry climate with bright sunshine; low humidity required during fruit ripening

stages.description: Multi-stemmed bushy shrub with glossy oblong-lanceolate leaves.
Showy bright scarlet tubular flowers bloom (Bahar treatment induces flush).
Globose fruits with persistent calyx pack hundreds of ruby-red juice arils.
Rind turns rich red or yellow-pink; makes metallic sound when tapped.

funFact: Pomegranates are hailed as sacred superfruits in Siddha medicine, celebrated across Tamil Nadu for their antioxidant punicalagins that purify the blood!
basicPractices: Train to 3–4 main stems from base; prune ground suckers continuously.
Induce uniform flowering via regulated water stress (Bahar treatment).
Spray Calcium Chloride @ 2 g/L during fruit growth to avoid rind splitting.
tamilDisease: மாதுளை பாக்டீரியா கருகல் / எண்ணெய் புள்ளி நோய்
symptoms: Dark brown to black angular water-soaked oily spots on leaves
Diagnostic brown to black 'L' or 'Y' shaped cracks on developing fruit rind
Infected branches develop stem cankers, crack open, and snap easily
cause: Bacterial pathogen Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. punicae spreading via wind-driven rain and pruning tools.
prevention: Spray Streptocycline @ 0.5 g/L + Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5 g/L at 10-day intervals
Paste stem cuts immediately with Bordeaux paste (10%) after pruning
Sterilize pruning shears in 70% alcohol between cuts

name: Amla (Nellikai)
soilType: Light sandy loams, gravelly red soils, and sodic soils (pH 6.5 – 9.0)
sunlight: Full hot sunshine; extraordinarily drought-hardy semi-arid tree

stages.description: Feathery pinnate-like branchlets resemble compound leaves with flaking grey bark.
Clusters of minute yellowish flowers bloom on bare branchlets.
Fertilised ovaries enter dormancy then swell rapidly after autumn rains.
Globular six-ribbed greenish-yellow fruits turn translucent; packed with vitamin C.

funFact: Ancient Tamil Sangam queen Avvaiyar was gifted a rare immortal Amla fruit by king Athiyaman, celebrated for holding twenty times more vitamin C than oranges!
basicPractices: Plant TNAU-developed high-yielding varieties like NA 7, Krishna, and Kanchan.
Prune dead twiggy branchlets annually after harvest.
Mulch tree basins with dry organic matter to conserve root moisture.
symptoms: Small circular purplish-brown spots on leaflets and tender green fruits
Pustules erupt into powdery rust-colored spores that cause fruit scabbing
Severely affected fruits crack, drop prematurely, and fail to mature
cause: Fungal pathogen Ravenelia emblicae proliferating in humid post-monsoon weather.
prevention: Foliar spray with Wettable Sulphur 80% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Mancozeb @ 2.0 g/L
Spray twice at 15-day intervals during fruit development (July–August)
Prune dense internal shoots to allow morning breeze circulation

name: Neem Tree (Veppamaram)
soilType: Extremely versatile; thrives in rocky, gravelly, saline, and degraded soils
sunlight: Full scorching tropical sun; celebrated natural air purifier and biopesticide
majorTNRegions: Widespread across all 38 districts of Tamil Nadu

stages.description: Pinnate serrated green leaves; deeply furrowed dark brown bark.
Panicles of fragrant star-like white flowers bloom alongside fresh tender red shoots.
Small ellipsoidal green berries cluster thickly in leaf axils.
Ripe berries turn yellow, containing azadirachtin-rich seeds for neem oil extraction.

funFact: Neem is revered as the 'Village Pharmacy of India'; its tender flower blossoms are traditionally cooked into bitter-sweet 'Veppam Poo Rasam' on Tamil New Year's Day!
basicPractices: Crush neem seeds to produce cold-pressed neem oil (NSKE 5%) for organic pest control.
Use neem cake as organic soil fertilizer to suppress root-knot nematodes.
Plant as windbreak and shade avenue tree around farm field boundaries.
symptoms: Drying and withering of leaves and twigs starting from the branch tip downward ('Die-Back')
Leaves turn chlorotic brown, curl up, and fall off, leaving skeletal bare branches
Inflorescences turn black and rot before setting fruit
cause: Fungal pathogen Phomopsis azadirachtae attacking during warm humid monsoon flushes.
prevention: Prune affected branches 5 cm below the dead margin and burn infected twigs
Spray Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L or Mancozeb @ 2.0 g/L during new shoot emergence
Paint cut branch ends with Bordeaux paste (10%)

name: Rose Plant (Roja)
soilType: Rich, fertile, well-drained loamy soil rich in organic humus with pH 6.0 – 6.8
sunlight: Minimum 6 hours of bright morning sun; sheltered from scorching heatwave winds

stages.description: Pruned canes burst with vibrant reddish young shoots.
Serrated glossy leaflets develop on thorny canes.
Sepals peel back revealing folded velvety scented petals.
Cut at tight bud stage for Chennai, Bangalore, and export markets.

funFact: Hosur in Krishnagiri district is India's leading cut-rose export hub, exporting millions of 'Taj Mahal' and 'Grand Gala' Dutch roses worldwide for Valentine's Day!
basicPractices: Perform annual pruning in October, cutting canes 45 cm above ground to an outward-facing bud.
Apply 10 kg FYM + 50 g rose fertilizer mixture per bush post-pruning.
Spray Neem oil 1% or Azoxystrobin @ 1 ml/L to ward off powdery mildew and black spot.
symptoms: Fringed circular black spots on upper leaf surfaces surrounded by bright yellow chlorosis
Infected leaves drop prematurely, leaving lower canes completely stripped of foliage
Stems develop purple-red blistered cankers that weaken flowering canes
cause: Fungal spores of Diplocarpon rosae spreading through splashing water drops and high relative humidity.
prevention: Foliar spray with Trifloxystrobin + Tebuconazole @ 0.5 g/L or Mancozeb @ 2.0 g/L
Water at the base of the plant using drip lines; never wet rose leaves in the evening
Collect and burn all fallen infected black-spotted leaves

name: Jasmine Plant (Malligai)
soilType: Well-drained sandy loam and red loam rich in organic matter with pH 6.5 – 7.5
sunlight: Warm, sunny days; minimum 6–8 hours of intense direct sunshine

stages.description: Annual pruning in December induces fresh productive lateral shoots.
Opposite ovate glossy green leaves cover dense bushy shrub.
Tight, firm, pure white buds cluster in cymes.
Picked in early morning; opens at dusk releasing divine aroma.

funFact: 'Madurai Malli' holds a world-famous Geographical Indication (GI) tag, celebrated for its unique thick petals, long shelf-life, and intoxicating heavenly fragrance!
basicPractices: Prune bushes annually in last week of November to 45 cm height to trigger peak summer flowering.
Apply 10 kg FYM + 120 g Urea, 240 g Superphosphate, and 240 g Potash per bush annually.
Harvest tight white buds early in the morning before 8 AM for prime market fragrance.
symptoms: Reddish-brown circular to irregular spots on leaves expanding into dark necrotic blights
Infected floral buds turn brown, shrivel, and fail to open
Severe canopy defoliation drastically reducing daily flower bud yield
cause: Airborne fungal pathogen Alternaria jasmini thriving in warm temperatures with rain showers.
prevention: Foliar spray with Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5 g/L
Spray twice at 15-day intervals during new vegetative flushes
Maintain clean bush aeration through proper pruning

name: Hibiscus (Semparuthi)
soilType: Fertile, loose, well-drained loams rich in compost; slightly acidic to neutral
sunlight: Full bright sunshine; requires high light to produce continuous vibrant blooms
majorTNRegions: Widespread across all districts; extensive in home gardens & temple farms

stages.description: Semi-hardwood stem cuttings root quickly in potting compost.
Deep green serrated glossy leaves form an evergreen bush 1.5–3 m tall.
Large tubular buds emerge singly in upper leaf axils.
Magnificent five-petaled trumpet flowers bloom with prominent protruding staminal column.

funFact: Red Hibiscus petals ('Semparuthi') are prized in traditional Tamil herbal hair oils for promoting lustrous hair growth and brewed into cooling herbal teas!
basicPractices: Prune lightly in spring to maintain compact bushy form and promote new flower buds.
Wash off white mealybug clusters with strong jet of water mixed with soap spray.
Apply vermicompost and neem cake every 3 months around the root zone.
symptoms: Severe upward and downward curling and crinkling of leaf margins
Thickening and swelling of veins on the lower leaf surface ('Enation')
Stunted branch internodes with deformed, drop-prone floral buds
cause: Begomovirus transmitted by the whitefly vector (Bemisia tabaci).
prevention: Foliar spray with Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5 ml/L or Neem oil 2% to control whiteflies
Prune and destroy severely distorted curled branches
Keep garden borders weed-free to eliminate wild host reservoirs

name: Marigold (Saamanthi)
soilType: Well-drained rich sandy loam and clay loam with pH 6.5 – 7.5
sunlight: Full, bright, unobstructed sunshine; shade causes leggy growth with few flowers

stages.description: Feathery pinnatisect leaves develop; ready for field transplanting.
Aromatic foliage branches profusely; root exude natural nematicides.
Globular floral heads develop on terminal peduncles.
Dense golden-orange and bright yellow flower heads picked every 3–4 days.

funFact: Marigold roots secrete alpha-terthienyl, a natural biochemical that destroys deadly root-knot nematodes, making it Tamil Nadu's favorite eco-friendly companion crop in vegetable fields!
basicPractices: Pinch terminal shoots at 30 DAT to induce dense bushy lateral flowering branches.
Intercrop with tomato, brinjal, or cotton as an eco-friendly nematode trap crop.
Harvest fully open flower heads in cool early morning hours.
symptoms: Minute circular brown spots on leaves that expand into large concentric necrotic patches
Infected flower petals develop water-soaked brown rot spots, turning into slimy mush
Premature drying and withering of flower buds before opening
cause: Airborne fungus Alternaria tagetica favored by warm humid weather with rain showers.
prevention: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Iprodione @ 1.5 g/L at first symptom
Avoid overhead irrigation during flowering to keep flower heads dry
Collect and destroy withered rotten flower heads

name: Tulsi (Holy Basil)
soilType: Fertile, loamy, well-aerated soil rich in organic humus with good drainage
sunlight: Full bright sunshine; minimum 5–6 hours of direct solar exposure daily
majorTNRegions: Cultivated in courtyards, temple gardens, and commercial medicinal farms statewide

stages.description: Minute aromatic seedlings establish; opposite ovate leaves develop.
Square purple or green stems branch into an aromatic medicinal shrub.
Purplish-white tubular flowers bloom along slender terminal verticillasters.
Top tender shoots and aromatic eugenol-rich leaves harvested for herbal tea.

funFact: Tulsi is revered as the 'Queen of Herbs' in Tamil households; its aromatic leaves release pure oxygen and eugenol essential oils with potent antiviral properties!
basicPractices: Pinch terminal flower spikes regularly to keep the plant in vigorous leafy vegetative growth.
Avoid overwatering; soggy soil causes root collar rot in Holy Basil.
Spray neem oil 1% for organic pest protection without toxic chemicals.
symptoms: Dark brown circular to irregular necrotic spots on sacred aromatic leaves
Lesions coalesce, causing leaf margins to curl and shed prematurely
Stems develop dark streaks during wet, humid weather
cause: Airborne fungus Alternaria alternata proliferating under prolonged leaf dampness.
prevention: Spray bio-fungicide Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/L or Neem oil 1%
Ensure full morning sunshine and well-drained pot aeration
Remove and compost lower infected leaves

name: Aloe Vera
soilType: Well-drained sandy loam, gravelly red soils, and coastal sand; intolerant of waterlogging
sunlight: Full scorching sunlight; thick succulent CAM photosynthetic plant

stages.description: Rhizome offsets (pups) root easily in dry loose soil.
Forms a dense stemless rosette of thick fleshy lanciform leaves.
Thick serrated spiny leaves store rich polysaccharides and soothing gel.
Mature outer fleshy leaves harvested cleanly at stem base.

funFact: Aloe Vera ('Sothu Katrazhai') is celebrated in Siddha medicine as a supreme skin healer, natural coolant, and digestive detoxifier, cultivated extensively in coastal Tamil Nadu!
basicPractices: Plant root suckers on raised ridges spaced 60 x 50 cm.
Water sparingly; allow soil to dry completely between irrigation cycles.
Harvest only mature lowest outer leaves, leaving inner rosette to grow.
symptoms: Distinct circular black to dark-brown spots surrounded by pale chlorotic rings on thick succulent leaves
Spots become sunken and hard, with dark spore pustules in the center
Severe infection disfigures fleshy leaves, rendering commercial cosmetic gel unusable
cause: Fungal pathogen Uromyces aloes spreading under cool, humid conditions and overcrowding.
prevention: Foliar spray with Mancozeb @ 2.0 g/L or Wettable Sulphur @ 2.5 g/L at first appearance
Avoid overhead watering that wets the rosette heart
Prune and destroy severely spotted outer succulent leaves

name: Curry Leaf Plant (Kariveppilai)
soilType: Deep, fertile red sandy loam and alluvial soil with good drainage
sunlight: Bright warm sunshine; thrives in semi-arid and tropical climates

stages.description: Develops into a small aromatic tree with dark grey bark.
Periodic pruning at 1 meter height forces dense aromatic leafy flushes.
Highly aromatic shiny green leaflets rich in volatile essential oils.
Entire leafy shoots harvested and bunched for Chennai and export markets.

funFact: Mettupalayam in Coimbatore district is the 'Curry Leaf Hub of India', sending fresh aromatic bundles daily to markets across India and the Middle East!
basicPractices: Prune bushes periodically at 1 meter height to trigger fresh, tender, aromatic leafy flushes.
Apply 20 kg FYM and 150 g Urea per bush after every harvest flush.
Spray Neem oil 2% or bio-pesticides to control psyllids without chemical pesticide residues.
symptoms: Minute dark brown to black circular spots scattered across aromatic leaflets
Spots coalesce, turning leaf tips yellow and causing premature leaflet defoliation
Blemished leaflets are rejected in fresh culinary markets
cause: Fungal pathogen Cercospora murrayae spreading during warm rainy weather.
prevention: Foliar spray with Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1.0 g/L or Mancozeb @ 2.0 g/L with 15-day pre-harvest waiting period
Spray safe bio-fungicide Trichoderma viride @ 5.0 g/L for residue-free culinary herbs
Thin congested branches to improve interior sunlight and aeration

name: Coriander (Kothamalli)
soilType: Rich, fertile, well-drained loamy and black cotton soils rich in organic matter
sunlight: Bright mild sunshine; hot scorching heat triggers premature bolting

stages.description: Split 'dhania' mericarps sprout tender feathery aromatic cotyledons.
Tender fan-lobed aromatic green leaves ready for culinary fresh bunch harvest.
Feathery filiform leaves top slender stems bearing white or pale pink compound umbels.
Globular aromatic ribbed seeds turn from green to light golden-brown.

funFact: Coriander is a dual-purpose culinary marvel: its fresh green leaves ('Kothamalli Thazhai') garnish every Tamil dish, while its aromatic dried seeds ('Dhania') form the backbone of sambar powder!
basicPractices: Gently crush whole coriander seeds into two split halves (mericarps) before sowing to double germination speed.
Soak split seeds in water for 12 hours with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg seed.
Harvest fresh greens 35–45 days after sowing before high temperatures cause bolting.
symptoms: White powdery talcum-like patches appear on feathery leaves and umbel flower heads
Powdery coating covers the entire plant, causing leaves to yellow, wither, and dry up
Umbels fail to set seeds, or seeds become shrivelled, blackened, and unmarketable
cause: Airborne fungal pathogen Erysiphe polygoni favored by cool dry days with high morning humidity during flowering.
prevention: Foliar spray with Wettable Sulphur 80% WP @ 2.0 g/L or Dinocap @ 1.0 ml/L at flowering onset
Dust fine sulphur powder @ 20 kg/ha in early morning hours
Cultivate powdery mildew tolerant varieties like CO 4 and Sadhana

name: Teak Tree (Thekku)
soilType: Deep, fertile, well-drained alluvial and moist red loamy soils with high calcium; hates waterlogging
sunlight: Demanding full solar exposure; large deciduous leaves capture high sunlight

stages.description: Root stumps or tissue culture saplings sprout vigorous straight leader shoots.
Pruned clean cylindrical bole reaches 10–18 meters height with massive opposite leaves.
Golden-brown heartwood rich in natural preservative tectoquinones matures.
Valuable timber harvested for luxury furniture, shipbuilding, and architectural woodwork.

funFact: Teak timber contains natural natural silica and aromatic oils (tectoquinone) that make it 100% immune to termites, weathering, and fungal rot for centuries!
basicPractices: Plant root-shoot stumps (1 cm thickness) in 45 cm³ pits spaced 3 x 3 m.
Prune side branches cleanly along the main stem up to 6 meters height to produce knot-free timber.
Dig contour trenches to harvest rainwater on farm boundary agroforestry plantings.
symptoms: Thousands of tiny yellowish-brown rust pustules on the lower surface of massive teak leaves
Leaves turn brownish-grey and brittle, drying up prematurely across the canopy
Larvae skeletonize the green parenchymal tissue, leaving only bare lace-like leaf veins
cause: Fungal pathogen Olivea tectonae combined with seasonal leaf skeletonizer caterpillar attacks post-monsoon.
prevention: Spray Mancozeb @ 2.0 g/L or Wettable Sulphur @ 2.5 g/L on young agroforestry saplings
Apply bio-insecticide Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) @ 2.0 g/L to suppress skeletonizer caterpillars
Collect and burn fallen dried leaves in autumn to destroy overwintering pupae and fungal spores
